author.name: Kenneth Grahame
author.biography: Born in Edinburgh, he worked at the Bank of England for nearly thirty years, and the book grew from stories he told and wrote to his young son.

hook.text: What pulls you away from home, and what brings you back?

paragraphs: One spring morning the Mole throws down his whitewash brush and leaves his underground house for the open air. By the end of the day he has found a river, which he has never seen before, and a friend in the Water Rat, who lives on its bank and believes nothing is half as worthwhile as messing about in boats.

Through the Rat he meets the rest of the river bank: the gruff, wise Badger, who lives deep in the Wild Wood and cannot stand society, and Toad of Toad Hall, good-natured, boastful and carried away by every new craze. When Toad discovers motor-cars, his friends have to decide how far they will go to save him from himself.

Between Toad's escapades the book slows down. The Mole, homesick on a winter night, catches the scent of his old burrow; the Rat and the Mole go looking for a lost young otter; and a seafaring rat passing through tempts the Rat with stories of the sea and the ports of the south.
The book is about friendship and home, and about the restlessness that pulls against both. Read it for the river and the turning seasons as much as for what happens.

orientation.text: Twelve chapters. Toad's adventures alternate with quieter chapters along the river. The animals talk, wear clothes, live in houses and deal with humans on the road, and nobody finds that strange.
